question: Does price-per-square-foot actually track the real cost drivers of an illuminated channel-letter sign job?
summary: Derived a four-term cost function (fixed design/permit/mobilization + perimeter-driven trim/labor + area-driven face/LED/PSU + install difficulty) predicting that flat $/sqft underprices small, ornate, or hard-to-access jobs. Industry sources confirm the real estimating structure matches: per-letter height-tier pricing, per-linear-foot raceway pricing, an explicit 20-40% intricacy surcharge, and separate electrical line items -- $/sqft is buyer-facing shorthand, not the shop's actual model.
